edges.effect_quant: In genotype-stratified intervention work, 5-MTHF lowered homocysteine by about 19.4% from baseline and appears to bypass at least part of the metabolic bottleneck relevant to MTHFR 677TT carriers.
edges.population: adults or women of reproductive age carrying MTHFR C677T variants, especially TT
edges.mechanism: Methylfolate provides the biologically active 5-MTHF form directly, bypassing the reduced enzymatic conversion capacity associated with the thermolabile MTHFR 677TT genotype. That gives it a mechanistic advantage over folic acid when the main problem is impaired folate activation rather than low folate intake alone.
edges.summary: Methylfolate is a plausible targeted intervention for MTHFR 677TT-related folate metabolism issues, but the evidence is still narrower than popular supplement marketing suggests. Randomized and genotype-aware studies support improved folate or homocysteine handling, yet hard clinical outcome data remain limited and condition-specific.
edges.caveats: This edge uses a broad outcome label because the literature spans biochemical response and reproductive settings more than a single disease endpoint. It should be read as an emerging precision-nutrition signal for TT carriers, not as proof that 5-MTHF is universally superior for every folate-related outcome.

evidence.citation: Hekmatdoost A et al 2015 PLoS One
evidence.notes: Methyltetrahydrofolate vs Folic Acid Supplementation in Idiopathic Recurrent Miscarriage with Respect to Methylenetetrahydrofolate Reductase C677T and A1298C Polymorphisms: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
